phrases:a-bit-informal-degree.title: a bit：有点（口语程度副词）
phrases:a-bit-informal-degree.explanation: a bit 是口语化的程度副词，表示“有点、略微”，与 a little bit 意思相近但更简短；修饰形容词、副词、动词，接不可数名词时用 a bit of。
phrases:a-bit-informal-degree.source: The movie was a bit long.
phrases:a-bit-informal-degree.example: It's a bit cold outside, so take a jacket.

phrases:a-price-to-pay.title: a price to pay
phrases:a-price-to-pay.explanation: A fixed collocation meaning a cost, loss, or consequence accepted in exchange for something gained. 'A big price to pay' = a heavy cost. The infinitive 'to pay' post-modifies 'price'. Core pattern: pay a price for something / there is a price to pay for sth.
phrases:a-price-to-pay.source: a pretty big price to pay
phrases:a-price-to-pay.example: There is a price to pay for success, and it is called discipline.

phrases:a-wide-range-of.title: a wide range of（种类繁多的/广泛多样的）
phrases:a-wide-range-of.explanation: 意为'大量的、种类繁多的、覆盖范围很广的'，置于名词前，表示某个集合/范围内包含很多不同类型的东西。结构：a + (wide/broad/full) + range + of + 复数可数名词或不可数名词。近义表达：a wide/broad variety of、a wide selection of、plenty of。正式与口语皆可用，略偏正式。
phrases:a-wide-range-of.example: The store offers a wide range of products. 这家店提供种类繁多的商品。

phrases:after-all-means-in-spite-of-ever.title: after all：表示毕竟、终究，不是“后来”
phrases:after-all-means-in-spite-of-ever.explanation: after all 是固定短语，表示“毕竟、说到底、终究”，用于给出理由或修正预期，与时间先后无关；不能用它表示“后来”。
phrases:after-all-means-in-spite-of-ever.source: Don't be too hard on her — she's only been here a week, after all.
phrases:after-all-means-in-spite-of-ever.example: I thought the test would be easy, but it was hard after all.

phrases:after-fixed-phrases-look-after-n.title: after 的三个高频固定搭配：look after / name after / be after
phrases:after-fixed-phrases-look-after-n.explanation: look after 表示照顾；name A after B 表示以 B 命名 A；be after something 表示追赶、谋求或寻找。这三个短语里的 after 都不是时间先后。
phrases:after-fixed-phrases-look-after-n.source: She looks after her grandmother; the street is named after a poet; the police are after him.
phrases:after-fixed-phrases-look-after-n.example: He is after a promotion, and his manager looks after the whole team.

phrases:all-set.title: all set：一切就绪 / 搞定
phrases:all-set.explanation: all set 是非正式口语惯用语：set 在此是形容词，意为 ready / arranged，all 加强语气；意思是「一切都准备好了、安排妥当了、没问题了」，常用于告知别人事情已经搞定、可以放心，语气亲切、带安抚意味，美式英语高频。常见场景：点餐后服务员问 Are you all set?（点好了吗）、出发前确认 All set?、向对方保证 All set — we've taken care of everything。它只描述「人或整体安排」已经就绪的状态，不能像 deliver / send 那样接 to + 地点表示「送到某地」：the luggage was all set to the hotel lobby 缺真正的动作动词，应说 was delivered to the hotel lobby。
phrases:all-set.example: Are you all set? — All set: the tickets are booked and the luggage was delivered to the hotel.

phrases:back-east-us.title: back east
phrases:back-east-us.explanation: 从美国西部或中部的视角指美国东部；back 带有回望来处或既有地域视角的意味，通常不译为“回到东部”。
phrases:back-east-us.source: Old-timers used it to describe a man who had just arrived from one of the big cities back east
phrases:back-east-us.example: She grew up back east but now lives in Arizona.

phrases:be-home-to.title: be home to — 是……的家园/所在地
phrases:be-home-to.explanation: 固定搭配，表示某地/某物是某类人、动物或事物的家园、栖息地或所在地。主语通常是地点（国家、城市、地区、场馆），home 此处作名词，前不加冠词。常用于介绍性、说明性语境。
phrases:be-home-to.source: It's home to more than 50 distinct ethnic groups.
phrases:be-home-to.example: The rainforest is home to thousands of rare species. 这片雨林是数千种珍稀物种的家园。

phrases:can-t-stand-tolerate.title: can't stand + 名词/动名词（受不了…）
phrases:can-t-stand-tolerate.explanation: cannot/can't stand 表示“无法忍受”，后接名词或动名词（V-ing），一般不用 to do；主要用于否定与疑问语境。
phrases:can-t-stand-tolerate.source: I cannot stand the smell of smoke.
phrases:can-t-stand-tolerate.example: I can't stand people smoking next to me in restaurants.

phrases:clear-the-table-after-meal.title: clear the table：收拾餐桌
phrases:clear-the-table-after-meal.explanation: clear the table 表示饭后把盘子、杯子、餐具等从桌上收走，常用于家庭分工或餐后清理。
phrases:clear-the-table-after-meal.source: 改一下场景对话：不是你一句我一句，而是你直接把美国人常见的场景对话案例全展示给我
phrases:clear-the-table-after-meal.example: I’ll clear the table after breakfast.

phrases:come-on-in-invite-guest-inside.title: Come on in：快进来吧
phrases:come-on-in-invite-guest-inside.explanation: Come on in 是美式日常待客时很自然的进门邀请，语气亲切随意，比 Please enter 更生活化。
phrases:come-on-in-invite-guest-inside.example: Hey, come on in. Breakfast is almost ready.

phrases:dish-out.title: dish out：分发、给出（食物、批评、惩罚）
phrases:dish-out.explanation: dish out 的核心意思是把某物分发出去或给出去：可以是食物（dish out napkins），也常用于抽象事物，如建议、批评、惩罚或钱（The teacher dished out advice before the exam）。它的宾语是被分发或施加的内容（criticism、punishment、insults），不是承受批评的人；要说明对象用 dish out criticism to / at someone，或改写为 criticize others。用在批评、惩罚语境时，常带「不断给出、强硬施加」的语气。固定习语 can dish it out but can't take it 表示「会批评别人却受不了别人批评自己」，前后用 it 回指批评或玩笑，不能说 dish out others' voice 之类的宾语。
phrases:dish-out.source: Compare dish up and dish out
phrases:dish-out.example: She always dishes out criticism to her teammates, but she can't take it when they answer back.

phrases:dish-up.title: dish up：把饭菜盛好端上桌
phrases:dish-up.explanation: dish up 指把食物从锅或大盘里盛到盘子、碗里再端上桌，语气日常。它是可分短语动词：名词宾语可放在 up 前或后（dish up the rice / dish the rice up），代词宾语必须放中间（dish it up）。与 serve 的区别：serve 范围更宽，可指端菜、供应食物、招待客人或餐厅酒店供应某类食物（The hotel serves breakfast from seven to ten），语域更中性、更适合正式场景。与 plate 的区别：plate 强调把食物摆放在盘中并呈现外观，汤类通常用 serve 或 ladle，不用 plate。dish out 则是把东西分发出去，宾语多为内容而非「盛到盘里」，语义范围更宽。
phrases:dish-up.source: Now, to dish up something means to put food on a dish for someone to eat
phrases:dish-up.example: She dished up the soup, while her sister served the drinks.

phrases:get-down-to-brass-tacks.title: get down to brass tacks：直入主题（美式口语）
phrases:get-down-to-brass-tacks.explanation: get down to brass tacks 是美式口语习语，意为'停止铺垫、直接谈正题/关键实质'，语气比 get down to business 更随意、更强调'谈要点本身'。常见于会议、谈判、朋友间催促进入重点。tacks 为黄铜平头钉，其确切词源有争议（常见联想为布匹店按钉售布），但作为记忆联想即可。
phrases:get-down-to-brass-tacks.source: OK, let's get down to brass tacks.
phrases:get-down-to-brass-tacks.example: Enough small talk — let's get down to brass tacks and talk about money.

phrases:get-down-to-business.title: get down to business：开始办正事
phrases:get-down-to-business.explanation: get down to business 是固定习语，意思是停止闲聊或铺垫，开始着手处理真正重要、实际的事务。此处的 business 不是'生意'，而是'the matter/task at hand'（手头正事）。get down to 表示从闲聊/准备状态转入专注执行。语气中性偏口语，常见于会议、工作、谈判开场。可替换为 get to work、cut to the chase（更随意）。
phrases:get-down-to-business.example: We've had enough small talk — let's get down to business.

phrases:get-the-plates-fetch-or-prepare.title: get the plates：去拿/准备盘子
phrases:get-the-plates-fetch-or-prepare.explanation: 日常口语里 get something 常表示去拿、取来或准备某物，不只是字面上的“得到”；get the plates 在餐桌场景中通常是把盘子拿过来或准备好。
phrases:get-the-plates-fetch-or-prepare.source: Sure. I'll dish up the eggs while you get the plates.
phrases:get-the-plates-fetch-or-prepare.example: Could you get the cups while I pour the tea?

phrases:go-for-it-encouragement.title: go for it 鼓励别人放手去做
phrases:go-for-it-encouragement.explanation: 口语鼓励表达，意思是“放手去做吧/去争取吧/试试看”，当对方想做某事却犹豫时用来打气。go for 本义“去争取、去拿下”，it 虚指对方心里想的那件事，无需明说。可直接以祈使句使用：You've been training for months — go for it!
phrases:go-for-it-encouragement.example: You've been training for months — go for it!

phrases:go-on-with-activity.title: go on with：继续某项活动
phrases:go-on-with-activity.explanation: go on with + 名词表示继续进行某项活动，语气比 resume 更口语；go on doing 则表示继续做某个动作。
phrases:go-on-with-activity.source: Please go on with your presentation.
phrases:go-on-with-activity.example: After answering the question, the speaker went on with the presentation.

phrases:go-out-with-romantic-dating.title: go out with someone：与某人约会
phrases:go-out-with-romantic-dating.explanation: go out with someone 在恋爱语境中表示与某人约会或谈恋爱，不只是一起外出；上下文决定其含义。
phrases:go-out-with-romantic-dating.source: A young man may suffer from the green-eyed monster if his girlfriend begins going out with someone else
phrases:go-out-with-romantic-dating.example: Is she going out with Daniel?

phrases:go-sailing-activity-collocation.title: go sailing：去帆船航行 / 去坐帆船
phrases:go-sailing-activity-collocation.explanation: go sailing 是 go + -ing 结构，表示去做某项休闲或运动活动。sailing 强调驾驶或乘帆船在水上活动，不等同于泛泛地说乘船 travel by boat。
phrases:go-sailing-activity-collocation.example: We might go sailing this weekend if the weather stays clear.

phrases:have-sth-covered.title: have / get ... covered（一切已安排妥当、准备齐全）
phrases:have-sth-covered.explanation: 口语习语，表示所有必要的事项、准备工作或风险都已处理妥当，无需担心。get = have 的口语形式，cover 在此意为「覆盖到、应付得了」。
phrases:have-sth-covered.source: 用户输入：We've got our bases covered.
phrases:have-sth-covered.example: Don't worry about the venue — we've got that covered. 别担心场地，我们已经安排好了。

phrases:have-whole-life-ahead-of-someone.title: have your whole life ahead of you
phrases:have-whole-life-ahead-of-someone.explanation: 表示一个人未来还有很长的时间和许多可能性，常用于安慰、鼓励年轻人或表达对未来的期待。ahead of someone 在这里指未来尚未经历的日子，而非物理位置。
phrases:have-whole-life-ahead-of-someone.source: I've got my whole life ahead of me.
phrases:have-whole-life-ahead-of-someone.example: Don't worry about one setback; you have your whole life ahead of you.

phrases:help-yourself-food-offer.title: help yourself：请自取/随便吃
phrases:help-yourself-food-offer.explanation: help yourself 常用于主人请客人或家人自己拿食物、饮料，语气轻松自然，意思是不用客气、自己取用。
phrases:help-yourself-food-offer.source: 改一下场景对话：不是你一句我一句，而是你直接把美国人常见的场景对话案例全展示给我
phrases:help-yourself-food-offer.example: Help yourself to some toast and coffee.

phrases:hidden-world.title: hidden world — 隐秘世界/秘境
phrases:hidden-world.explanation: 固定的比喻式短语，指外界知之甚少、自成一方天地的世界（自然秘境、地下世界、奇幻世界等），常作标题或称呼使用。
phrases:hidden-world.example: Scientists explored a hidden world beneath the ice. → 科学家探索了冰层下隐藏的天地。

phrases:home-cooked.title: home-cooked（家常的、家里自己做的）
phrases:home-cooked.explanation: 复合形容词，指饭菜由家里亲手做出来，而不是餐馆、外卖或工厂预制。高频搭配：home-cooked meal / food / dinner / cooking。作定语必须带连字符（a home-cooked casserole），作表语同样写成形容词形式（The food is home-cooked.）；只有 home 作状语、cooked 作谓语时才拆开（I cooked it at home.）。与 homemade 的分工：homemade 泛指非工业量产、自己制作，可用于果酱、家具、礼物；home-cooked 只用于饭菜，并带「用心、有家的味道」的评价色彩。
phrases:home-cooked.example: Nothing beats a home-cooked meal after a week of takeout.

phrases:laid-back-relaxed.title: laid back / laid-back：随和、松弛、不紧张
phrases:laid-back-relaxed.explanation: Informal adjective describing a person, attitude, place or event that is calm, relaxed and easygoing, not easily stressed or agitated. Predicative use after be: He is laid back. Attributive use before a noun needs a hyphen: a laid-back attitude / a laid-back bar. It is the opposite of uptight, tense or high-strung. Note the spelling: laid (past participle of lay), not layed.
phrases:laid-back-relaxed.source: I'm pretty laid back and prefer a night of playing cards with friends rather than a loud and crazy dance party.
phrases:laid-back-relaxed.example: My boss has a laid-back management style; she rarely raises her voice.

phrases:later-on.title: later on：稍后、等会儿
phrases:later-on.explanation: 时间副词短语，表示“再晚一些的时候”，比单独的 later 更口语、更随意，常见于日常对话，句首或句尾均可。
phrases:later-on.source: We'll talk about that a little bit later on.
phrases:later-on.example: I'll finish the report later on. / 我等会儿再写完报告。

phrases:later-on-unspecified-future-time.title: later on：日后某个不确定的时间
phrases:later-on-unspecified-future-time.explanation: later on 比 later 更口语，强调“以后某个时候”（多指将来），常放句末或句首；指过去的先后顺序时用 later 或 afterwards 更自然。
phrases:later-on-unspecified-future-time.source: We can sort out the details later on.
phrases:later-on-unspecified-future-time.example: I'll explain the rest later on.

phrases:lovely-day-to.title: Lovely day to... / What a lovely day for...
phrases:lovely-day-to.explanation: Lovely day to go sailing. 是 It's a lovely day to go sailing. 的省略说法：口语、标题和随口感叹里常省去可从语境推断的主语和 be 动词，使表达更轻快。Lovely day to... 字面在评价天气，实际常带轻松的建议、邀请或感叹意味，相当于「天气这么好，很适合……」，语气友好、偏日常口语。to 后面必须接动词原形，to 不能省略，也不能把 outside 这类副词直接放在 to 后。感叹形式 What a lovely day for + 名词或 -ing 更有感情色彩，比 It's a good day for... 更强烈。
phrases:lovely-day-to.example: What a lovely day for a picnic — lovely day to grab a sandwich and eat in the park, isn't it?

phrases:make-a-pit-stop.title: make a pit stop（短暂停留）
phrases:make-a-pit-stop.explanation: 源自赛车运动（pit 为赛道维修区，赛车进站加油换胎），现口语中借指旅途中的短暂停留，常委婉指上厕所、买吃的或加油。字面意义与喻义有清晰关联：先进站再短暂停靠。
phrases:make-a-pit-stop.source: Do you think we can make a pit stop?
phrases:make-a-pit-stop.example: Let's make a pit stop before we hit the highway.（上高速前我们先停一下吧。）

phrases:make-yourself-at-home.title: Make yourself at home：别拘束
phrases:make-yourself-at-home.explanation: Make yourself at home 用来让客人在家里放松自在，语气友好，常用于朋友来访或主人招待客人。
phrases:make-yourself-at-home.example: Make yourself at home. Coffee is on the counter.

phrases:old-timers.title: old-timers
phrases:old-timers.explanation: 指在某地生活很久、熟悉当地旧事和传统的人；语气较口语，不只是泛指老人。
phrases:old-timers.source: Old-timers used it to describe a man who had just arrived from one of the big cities back east
phrases:old-timers.example: The old-timers still remember when this road was unpaved.

phrases:regret-to-say.title: regret to say
phrases:regret-to-say.explanation: A fixed formal phrase used to introduce unwelcome or apologistic news. 'I regret to say that...' signals the speaker is about to deliver something unpleasant. It uses regret + infinitive, reserved for formal or polite communication. Contrast with regret + gerund (regret saying/having said), which refers to a past action one wishes undone.
phrases:regret-to-say.source: I regret to say that sacrificing your personal life is a pretty big price to pay.
phrases:regret-to-say.example: We regret to inform you that your application has not been successful.

phrases:resume-activity-after-break.title: resume：休息后重新开始
phrases:resume-activity-after-break.explanation: resume 是较正式的动词，表示中断后重新开始某项活动，常接名词，如 resume the presentation、resume the meeting。
phrases:resume-activity-after-break.source: We resumed the presentation after a short break.
phrases:resume-activity-after-break.example: The committee resumed the discussion after lunch.

phrases:review-common-collocations.title: review 的常见搭配
phrases:review-common-collocations.explanation: 高频搭配包括 review notes（复习笔记）、review a document（审查文件）、write a review（写评论）和 under review（正在审查中）。
phrases:review-common-collocations.example: The application is still under review.

phrases:serve.title: serve：端上、供应（食物与饮料）
phrases:serve.explanation: serve 表示把饭菜或饮料端给、供应给别人：可以是端上桌、分给客人，也可以指餐厅或酒店供应某类食物（The hotel serves breakfast from seven to ten）；语域比 dish up 更中性，也更适合正式场景。接受者可用双宾结构 serve someone something，或用 to 引出（serve hot tea to the guests）；for + 人更像「为了客人、替客人」，并不表示端给他们。serve 也可以表示「为某人服务」，但不说 serve service：提供服务用 provide / offer / give service。表示「负责某事」用 be responsible for + 名词，不能用被动 be served for。
phrases:serve.example: The waiter served the soup to the guests, and the hotel provided excellent service all evening.

phrases:set-the-table-arrange-place-sett.title: set the table：摆餐具
phrases:set-the-table-arrange-place-sett.explanation: set the table 表示吃饭前把盘子、杯子、刀叉或餐巾等摆好，不是设置桌子，而是准备餐桌。
phrases:set-the-table-arrange-place-sett.source: 改一下场景对话：不是你一句我一句，而是你直接把美国人常见的场景对话案例全展示给我
phrases:set-the-table-arrange-place-sett.example: Could you set the table while I dish up the eggs?

phrases:steaming-forests-nature-writing.title: steaming forests：热带雨林的文学化写法
phrases:steaming-forests-nature-writing.explanation: steaming forests 是自然纪录片、探险文学和旅游写作中形容热带雨林（尤其亚马逊）的常用意象：湿热空气让水汽在树冠上升腾。强调环境的炎热与潮湿，比 jungle 更「具象、有画面感」。可搭配 jungle、rainforest、lowlands 等同场景词。
phrases:steaming-forests-nature-writing.example: Mist rose from the steaming forests at dawn.

phrases:talk-about.title: talk about + 话题：谈论
phrases:talk-about.explanation: 及物短语动词，about 是介词，后面接谈论的话题对象，常与 it/that、具体名词或 -ing 连用。讨论具体某件事用 talk about；更正式或商定某方案时用 discuss。
phrases:talk-about.source: We'll talk about that a little bit later on.
phrases:talk-about.example: Let's talk about the plan after lunch. / 我们午饭后聊聊这个计划吧。

phrases:tell-tales-of.title: tell tales of sth 讲述……的故事/记载……
phrases:tell-tales-of.explanation: tell tales of 是固定搭配，指'讲述/流传关于……的故事'，主语常是讲故事的人、旅行者或传奇；比 tell stories about 更书面，带传说/轶事色彩。
phrases:tell-tales-of.source: ...travellers to China have told tales of magical landscapes and surprising creatures.
phrases:tell-tales-of.example: Old books tell tales of dragons and lost kingdoms. (古书讲述着龙与失落王国的传说。)

phrases:ten-minutes-of-rest.title: ten minutes of rest：十分钟的休息
phrases:ten-minutes-of-rest.explanation: of 结构把‘休息’当成一个整体名词短语，十分钟只是长度说明。这个说法比直接写 ten minutes rest 更完整，也常用于强调时间量。
phrases:ten-minutes-of-rest.example: He needed ten minutes of rest before continuing.

phrases:there-is-no-way.title: There's no way (that)… — 强烈否定：绝不可能 / 绝对不干
phrases:there-is-no-way.explanation: 整体意思是「绝对没有这种可能」：既能表达强烈拒绝（这东西我不吃），也能表达难以置信（这个量我根本吃不下去）。后面接一个完整从句，口语里 that 常省略；no way 否定的是整件事发生的可能性，不是单个动作。语气强、偏非正式，日常口语和影视对白里高频。
phrases:there-is-no-way.source: There's no way I'm gonna eat this!
phrases:there-is-no-way.example: There's no way I'm gonna eat this!（这东西我绝对不吃！）

phrases:walk-the-dog.title: walk the dog（遛狗）
phrases:walk-the-dog.explanation: 固定搭配，意为“带狗出去散步/遛狗”。walk 在此作及物动词，直接带宾语 the dog。连读要点：walk 结尾的爆破音 /k/ 与 the 开头的 /ð/ 直接衔接、几乎不爆破（不完全爆破），the 弱读为 /ðə/，整句听感近似一个词 /wɔːkðədɒɡ/。
phrases:walk-the-dog.source: 用户提问 walk the dog 如何连读
phrases:walk-the-dog.example: I walk the dog every morning before breakfast.

phrases:weather-report-forecast-informat.title: weather report：天气预报 / 天气报告
phrases:weather-report-forecast-informat.explanation: weather report 指电视、手机、网站或广播上的天气信息。出海、徒步、露营等户外活动前常说 check the weather report，表示先确认天气情况。
phrases:weather-report-forecast-informat.source: I’ll check the weather report before we go.
phrases:weather-report-forecast-informat.example: Check the weather report before you leave for the mountains.

phrases:you-are-what-you-eat.title: You are what you eat
phrases:you-are-what-you-eat.explanation: 英语里最常用的健康谚语之一，字面是「你是你所吃的东西」，实际表达「吃什么、怎么吃，决定你的身体状态和精神状态」。它是整句当名词短语用的固定说法，不能改成 You eat what you are。日常语境里多用于劝人少吃加工食品、多吃天然食物，也常被调侃式使用（比如吃完炸鸡自嘲）。
phrases:you-are-what-you-eat.example: My trainer keeps saying, "You are what you eat" — so no more midnight chips for me.

phrases:you-are-what-you-x.title: You are what you + 动词 的可复用公式
phrases:you-are-what-you-x.explanation: 这个谚语可以被模板化，替换最后一个动词来表达「你的行为/选择塑造了你」：You are what you read / what you practice / what you spend time on。语气偏说理、格言式，适合总结、演讲、社交媒体感慨，不适合正式商务报告。
phrases:you-are-what-you-x.example: You are what you practice, not what you plan.
